description: Reference benchmark result from benchmarks/index.html, generated locally. Each operation was repeated 5 times and the reported value is the median; the numbers below come from two complete, independent runs, one right after the other, to check reproducibility — including the two biggest outliers (Minze/binding and Lit/clear).

environment.userAgent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/150.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

methodology.timing: performance.now() around the operation + a double microtask flush (doesn't include browser repaint; requestAnimationFrame is paused by Chrome in background tabs, which would make automated measurement impossible)

observations: Minze/Binding (~770-800ms): two-way binding isn't a documented Minze feature (see the methodology on the page); the implementation used re-renders the component's entire HTML string on every keystroke via on:input, which recreates the <input> itself on each of the 1000 changes — a real cost of that approach, not a native feature comparable to the others' data-model.

Lit/Clear 1000 rows (~1.4s): consistent across both runs, and orders of magnitude larger than creating those same 1000 rows (~10ms) or removing rows one at a time (~2ms). Lit's own documentation (https://lit.dev/docs/templates/lists/) notes that the repeat() directive is optimized for reordering/updating existing items, not for replacing the whole list at once — the 'clear everything at once' scenario appears to fall into that directive's non-optimized case.

Numbers shouldn't be read as 'X is N times faster than Y' outside the exact scenario measured — these are 8 batched synchronous operations, not real user interactions; see the full methodology note in benchmarks/index.html.
